body:
Reviewed the diff and the surrounding tree state. Nothing blocking from my side — it is purely additive, CI is green, and it follows the same shape as the other `oqa_agnostic` modules. Four things I would fix or clarify.

**The verification table links point at the wrong jobs.** On all five rows the link text and the link target are different jobs, and the targets are the older batch: `6230398` → `/tests/6230352`, `24515782` → `/tests/24513178`, `24515783` → `/tests/24513179`, `24515784` → `/tests/24513180`, `24515785` → `/tests/24513181`. Anyone following a link lands on a job that ran an earlier revision of the branch than the head being reviewed.

**`test_localectl_keymap_matches_vconsole` cannot fail for a product reason.** The `VC Keymap` line in `localectl status` is systemd-localed's parse of `/etc/vconsole.conf` — the same file `parse_vconsole_conf()` just read — so the assertion compares the file with itself. The one case where the effective keymap legitimately differs from the file is a `vconsole.keymap=` kernel command line override, and that is not what is being compared.

**`test_font_configured`'s docstring promises a guard that does not exist.** It says "this module is only scheduled on products that configure a console font", but the module's only guard is `has_ttys()`; there is no product, flavour or version predicate in the `.pm` or the YAML. That is harmless while the module lives only in `console_font_verification.yaml`, but it becomes load-bearing as soon as this is wired into a broad schedule: `FONT` is written by systemd-firstboot / systemd-localed / YaST / Agama, not by the package, so an image provisioned without them fails `test_font_configured` outright. Worth settling before the follow-up that promotes the module.

**The commit message describes a tree state that no longer existed when the commit was made.** "consoletest_setup runs check_console_font (lib/utils.pm) in every job" and "PR #26740 proposes to drop it" — #26740 merged at 06:31Z and this commit is dated 07:16Z. More importantly, both the message and the PR body read as if the needle check were gone. It is not: `check_console_font` is untouched in `lib/utils.pm` and is still called from `tests/console/console_reboot.pm:30`, which 34 files under `schedule/`, `products/` and `lib/` reach — JeOS via `lib/main_common.pm:1272`, `products/opensuse/main.pm:203`, and the HA rolling-update and migration schedules. #26740 narrowed the wide textmode path; it did not remove the check. Saying so explicitly would make the scope of this PR much easier to judge.

Two smaller notes I would not hold the PR for:

- `test_apply_font_succeeds` runs `systemd-vconsole-setup` unconditionally, so a SUT that did boot with an unapplied font gets repaired by this module and reports green — the same silent repair the PR body criticises, without the detection half. Its docstring's "changes no files" is also not quite right: systemd 257's `vconsole-setup.c` writes `/sys/module/vt/parameters/default_utf8` before the "All allocated VCs are currently busy" early return, and `KD_FONT_OP_SET`s the other allocated VCs. Neither undermines what the test claims to check; the docstring just overstates it.
- `font_candidates()` strips `.gz` but never re-appends a bare `.gz`, so a `FONT=` value naming a file like `foo.gz` with no `.psf`/`.psfu` infix resolves to nothing. I could not find a product that produces such a value — yast-country ships four and all four resolve — so this is theoretical.
